text: This service reads the asset, collateral, score and appraisal facts it needs only through the rwb-source-data contract, and keeps the FSD field names (v_ace_npa_asset.*, v_ace_collateral.*, v_ace_asset.*, v_ace_score.*) as the source field names that contract returns.
why: Architecture v5 (higher in the source precedence) makes the 30 views readable by rwb-source-data alone and says every other service asks it by REST or by a Temporal activity.
read: The FSD field catalog and integration points as a statement of which facts the take-on, the price and the round need, not of how they are read.
applied_in: Section 2.4 constraint 3; Section 5 CAP-S5-019; Section 6 FR-S5-001, FR-S5-002, FR-S5-017, FR-S5-044; Section 8.2; Section 9
confirm: Solution architect with P1, before wave 2 system test
impact: If a view stays readable by this service, the boundary test and the freshness guarantee would each need a second owner.

text: The asset record this product keeps is this service's own holding record in schema rwb_asset, keyed by the ACE asset key with no foreign key and no copied ACE column, and the ACE NPA asset itself stays read-only through the source-data contract.
why: Architecture v5 slides 18 and 41 give rwb_asset the assets taken on; the TSD calls the object an extension of the ACE asset and the Ownership Map lists no asset table.
read: TSD S5 'asset (EXTEND ACE Asset)' as the Workbench record built on the ACE asset rather than as a table owned by ACE.
applied_in: Section 2.3; Section 6 FR-S5-002, FR-S5-003; Section 8.1; Section 12 OQ-S5-02
confirm: Data architect with the ACE team, before the S5 DB story
impact: Two writers of one asset record would leave the holding age and the book value disagreeing.

text: The service holds five entity groups in schema rwb_asset: the asset holding record, the listing, the sale, the auction round with its bids, and the holding cost movement; only the listing and the sale have a row in the Ownership Map, and no physical table name is stated.
why: Architecture v5 names auction rounds and holding in the schema, the rules use round, bid and holding cost fields, and the map names two tables.
read: The TSD object set as a minimum and the Arch v5 schema description as the full set.
applied_in: Section 8.1; Section 10; Section 12 OQ-S5-03
confirm: Data architect, before the S5 DB story
impact: The migration and the boundary test cannot be written until the table set exists; no story is blocked by it.

text: AssetSold is published on rwb.asset.events.v1 as a CloudEvent 1.0 keyed by asset and case, consumed by rwb-payment and rwb-case, and its EV number is allocated in the event catalogue next version.
why: Architecture v5 slide 19 gives the event on the topic and slide 43 carries it in the '+' rows without a number.
read: The '+' row as an event in the catalogue whose number is not yet allocated.
applied_in: Section 9; Section 11 AC-S5-023; Section 12 OQ-S5-04
confirm: Solution architect, before wave 3 system test
impact: Without a catalogue row the consumer contract and the reporting read model cannot be tested end to end.

text: The four current operations are published under /api/recovery/asset/v1 with the ACE business key, and a round is written as a sub-resource of the listing; the architecture slide's POST /auction-rounds is read as the same resource named loosely.
why: DP-13 fixes the base per service, the Ownership Map rules the business-key paths as current, and slide 19 names the round without a parent path.
read: The three sources as one resource set described at three levels of detail.
applied_in: Section 6 FR-S5-028, FR-S5-029; Section 9; Section 12 OQ-S5-05
confirm: Solution architect, before the S5 contract story closes
impact: A different base or path form would change the gateway composite route and the screen client.

text: The requirement keeps BR-027's wording (a vendor by distance and capacity), states that the allocation rule in force decides between distance and capacity and the scorecard, and records the rule version and the reason with every allocation.
why: The FSD carries both texts and neither the rule package nor a decision resolves them.
read: BR-027 and FEAT-AST-14 as the requirement, and R-DIS-30 as the rule row the package may implement instead.
applied_in: Section 6 FR-S5-030; Section 11 AC-S5-017; Section 12 OQ-S5-06
confirm: Business analyst, S5 with the center of excellence analyst
impact: A wrong reading changes which of four vendors is instructed and the price the sale starts from.

text: The one action records the listing, its prices and its schedule and issues the publication to the auction channel through rwb-partner, and the HOME.SCB publication is recorded as an officer step with its date and reference until INT-27 exists.
why: REQ-S5-005 requires one action, and the TSD and the BRD both state that INT-27 is not available today.
read: REQ-S5-005 as the product behaviour and INT-27 as an interface that is not built yet.
applied_in: Section 2.3; Section 6 FR-S5-025, FR-S5-026; Section 9; Section 11 AC-S5-014
confirm: Solution architect with the integration lead, before wave 2 system test
impact: A promise of automatic HOME.SCB publication would fail at the first release.

text: The allocation and the vendor instruction are built against the published rwb-partner contract and its fake, so the wave 4 partner story does not block the wave 3 release, and the instruction is held until the contract answers.
why: Contract-first delivery is the delivery rule, and the dependency is a contract dependency rather than a build dependency.
read: FEAT-PRM-03 as the panel and instruction contract, not as code that must exist first.
applied_in: Section 10.4; Section 11 AC-S5-017; Section 12 OQ-S5-08
confirm: Solution architect with the S9 owner, before wave 3 release
impact: If the contract is not published at wave 3, the allocation can be recorded but no vendor can be instructed and no round can run.

text: The re-appraisal is ordered through the valuation owner's contract and the accepted value and its date are read back through rwb-source-data, with the 12-month interval and the monthly scan kept as the product behaviour.
why: Architecture v5 gives the valuations and the valuation order to rwb-valuation, and the Ownership Map rules the two asset valuation operations to S1.
read: SVAF and INT-11 as the appraisal source behind ACE ingestion rather than as an interface this service calls.
applied_in: Section 6 FR-S5-017, FR-S5-018, FR-S5-019; Section 9; Section 12 OQ-S5-09
confirm: Solution architect with the S1 owner, before wave 2 system test
impact: Without a drawn path the monthly re-appraisal cannot be demonstrated and the price would run on a stale value.

text: Every posting goes to rwb-payment through postProceeds, and this service records the result from ProceedsMatched; it holds no ALS interface and no general-ledger interface, and the cost of carry is passed with its period to the same call.
why: Architecture v5 gives the payment, the proceeds matching, the fees and the postings to rwb-payment and gives this service the postProceeds call and the ProceedsMatched event.
read: The FSD's ALS and GL integration points as the posting outcome rather than as an interface of this service.
applied_in: Section 6 FR-S5-011, FR-S5-039; Section 9; Section 11 AC-S5-021
confirm: Solution architect with the P8 owner, before wave 3 system test
impact: Two writers of one posting would break the daily reconciliation to the ledger.

text: The route recommendation and the price proposal are decisions of the disposal rule set; where an agent proposes, it is reached only through the rwb-agent contract, waits at most 60 s, falls back to the rule result and leaves a run record.
why: DP-20 makes the agent reachable only through the rwb-agent contract and the slide 13 matrix gives this service no P10 cell.
read: The two rule rows that name a pricing agent as an option that the rule answer does not depend on.
applied_in: Section 6 FR-S5-021; Section 7 NFR-S5-004; Section 9; Section 12 OQ-S5-11
confirm: Solution architect with the model risk officer, before wave 2 system test
impact: An agent without a contract and a run record would make the price proposal untraceable.

text: The disposal rules are versioned data rows evaluated in process, the FSD's named R-DIS rows are the requirement, and the package code, the remaining rules and the 40-state list arrive with the Phase 2 rule package in rwb-decision.
why: The TSD states 72 rules over 40 states and prints 26, the FSD prints about 40, and the design names the package as Phase 2 with no code.
read: The rule rows the FSD carries as the behaviour this release must show, and the package as governance that follows.
applied_in: Section 5; Section 6 FR-S5-007, FR-S5-020 to FR-S5-036; Section 10.5; Section 12 OQ-S5-12
confirm: Center of excellence analyst with P7, before wave 2 release
impact: A decision taken on an unpublished rule set cannot be replayed against its version.

text: The stock balance owner is the NPA and asset manager role held as versioned reference data until Q-009 answers, and the monthly balance is refused where no owner role is in force.
why: BR-012 requires one named owner, the FSD names the NPA and asset manager as primary, and Q-009 is open.
read: The primary role of A2.6 as the owner role until the business names one.
applied_in: Section 6 FR-S5-013, FR-S5-014; Section 12 OQ-S5-13
confirm: Head of NPA, before wave 2 release
impact: A balance with no owner is the control failure the requirement exists to remove.

text: Every floor limit and approval level is read at run time from the versioned delegation table of rwb-access, the three amounts and the three percentages of the design slide are carried as stated, and the direction of the test is held open until DL18 and Q-001 answer.
why: DL18 and Q-001 leave the limits open and the comparison signs are unreadable in the extract.
read: The ladder as a statement of which level approves a floor at which size and which percentage, without reading a direction that is not legible.
applied_in: Section 2.4 constraint 7; Section 6 FR-S5-022, FR-S5-024; Section 7 NFR-S5-013; Section 12 OQ-S5-14
confirm: Risk with the product heads, before wave 2 release
impact: A limit read backwards would either let too low a floor through or stop every sale.

text: Sale prices, values, floors and cost amounts are [SENSITIVE_FINANCIAL], bidder and customer identity are [PII], vendor and partner data are [CONFIDENTIAL], and the retention periods stay open.
why: NFR-047 requires a classification per record, NFR-028 and NFR-031 leave the periods open, and the S5 field catalog marks every field as not personal data.
read: The classification scheme of the Non Functional Specification as the handling rule for this product's records.
applied_in: Section 8.1; Section 8.3; Section 12 OQ-S5-15
confirm: Compliance and PDPA officer, before wave 2 release
impact: An unclassified record cannot be masked, retained or produced to a court on a stated basis.

text: This document stays at status Draft with an empty approval table; the missing Product Owner and FDA approval is carried as an assumption and not as an answer.
why: The realignment run has no human verification stop and the BRD carries no dated decision for this PRD.
read: Rules R1 U8 and R9 as the instruction to record the missing approval and continue.
applied_in: Section 1.1; Section 13
confirm: Product Owner and FDA, after this run
impact: Nothing downstream may treat this PRD as approved until the table is signed.

text: The inherited history carries FSD S5 version 3 in full and marks versions 1 and 2 as not specified in the sources read.
why: Only the v3 change note is in the source and the earlier archives were not converted for this WP.
read: The document control table as the authoritative version history.
applied_in: Section 1.3
confirm: Business analyst, S5, if an ID continuity question is raised
impact: A missing early change note would show only if an ID turns out to have moved between v1 and v3.

text: The statutory notice is raised through the rwb-comms contract with its proof of delivery read back as an event, and every photograph, inspection report and transfer document is stored through the rwb-document contract.
why: Architecture v5 gives notices to rwb-comms and documents to rwb-document, and slide 37 allows Blob WORM through rwb-document only.
read: WIN and the document references of the FSD as the delivery outcome rather than as interfaces of this service.
applied_in: Section 6 FR-S5-008, FR-S5-009, FR-S5-015, FR-S5-037; Section 9; Section 12 OQ-S5-18
confirm: Solution architect with the P5 and P6 owners, before wave 2 system test
impact: A notice served without a stored proof is a take-on that cannot be defended and a document with no custody trail.

text: MSG-P1-001, MSG-P4-002, MSG-P7-003 and MSG-GEN-001 are shown from the catalogues of the services that own them, MSG-S5-001 and MSG-S5-002 come from this module's catalogue, and the Thai and English wording is settled with the business lead under DL10.
why: Four of the six messages are shared and DL10 leaves every label and message to the business lead with Legal and Compliance.
read: The message column of the FSD rule tables as the wording this product must show, not as a catalog this service owns.
applied_in: Section 6 FR-S5-005, FR-S5-019, FR-S5-024, FR-S5-044; Section 7 NFR-S5-027; Section 12 OQ-S5-19
confirm: Business analyst, S5 with the business lead, before wave 2 release
impact: A second copy of another service's message would drift from its source catalogue.

text: The service is sized on the case volume and the NPA book of NFR-001 until the asset, round and holding cost volumes are given, and the missing volume blocks the performance test only.
why: No S5 source states an asset, round or cost volume and NFR-001 states cases only.
read: NFR-001 as the upper bound of the population this service serves.
applied_in: Section 7 NFR-S5-005; Section 11.3; Section 12 OQ-S5-20
confirm: Solution architect with the data product owner, before wave 2 release
impact: A size taken from the wrong population would show only under auction load.

text: This is the first PRD of the S5 family, so version 1 is the next version in the folder and no earlier PRD is superseded.
why: The PRD folder holds no S5 file and the family's highest version is therefore zero.
read: Rules R8.2 as the versioning rule, applied to a family that does not yet exist.
applied_in: Section 1.1; Section 1.2
confirm: Document controller, at the next version
impact: None beyond the file name.

text: The release dates are copied unchanged and marked tentative: Epic 1 30 November 2026, Epic 3 31 January 2027 and Epic 4 28 February 2027, and this service is created in wave 2 with E3, so the E3 slice raises no wave conflict while the E4 stories sit in wave 3.
why: Rules R1 U7 and R5.6 keep the earlier of the business-epic wave and the service wave, and the BRD section 8 dates are tentative.
read: The BRD release plan and the wave map as the release plan of this product.
applied_in: Section 1.1; Section 10
confirm: Programme manager, at each release
impact: A date treated as fixed would be reported as a slip the sources never set.

text: Every owner named in this document is a role or a service code taken from the Ownership Map or from the service catalogue, and no person is named anywhere.
why: Rule 4 of the run rules and R1 U3 forbid a named person, and the Ownership Map is the owner register.
read: The Ownership Map services, endpoints, events, jobs and workflows as the owner set of this product.
applied_in: Section 1.1; Section 3; Section 9; Section 13
confirm: None needed
impact: None.

text: REQ-S5-001 to REQ-S5-010 are both the FSD requirement IDs and the program requirement IDs, and the BRD requirements that name this service are BR-010 to BR-014 and BR-026 to BR-030.
why: Program v5 section 5.12 and FSD S5 'Requirements served' carry the same ten IDs, and the BRD Epics 3 to 8 v1 names the S5 features in those ten BR rows.
read: The requirement IDs as stable across the two documents, so one ID is cited once and traces to both.
applied_in: Section 6; Section 11.2
confirm: Business analyst, S5
impact: A renumbered requirement would break the trace to the BRD and to the backlog.
